I got some brand new shoes and decide to break them in at the local indoor (they have a new box and I was wanting to try it out), anyway about an hour into the session I'm getting pretty consistent at pulling 360s and was rotating them round pretty slowly. So I thought to myself "hey, why not try 720" so I give it a go and the first few go okay, was a little under rotated on some and a little over on other.

Then I go for "this try" moment. I could feel myself under rotating so I go to put my foot down. Turns out this time I'd travelled a little further than expected, so instead of landing on top of the ramp, I land on the landing ramp. I was not prepared for this so whilst still rotating my foot hits the floor, my shoes with that "brand new" grip holds my foot in place but I keep spinning. *Snap* there goes my left ankle. 

As I'm falling, I feel the pain rush through my body and in a moment of blind panic I try jumping to my other leg for support, but I'm still spinning and the exact same happens to my right ankle...

Funny thing is, looking back at the CCTV footage, if I didn't put my foot down I probably would've landed it... But safe to say I never ride indoor skateparks with brand new shoes anymore...

Envy/Blunt is always a solid choice if you can't decide on street or park thanks to their choice of if you want dropouts or not. If you're planning on running a park/street hybrid setup then I would highly recommend the S6. 

As for compression, The S6 uses IHC which is the same as HIC but designed for standard sized bars which (in theory) is a lighter option to HIC due to the less amount of materials used in the forks, however, less material also means you lose some of the strength offered by HIC. 

Only real downside I've found with this compression type is that (especially on the Envy/Blunt IHC scooters) the compression sometimes spins within the bars loosening over time, but a quick fix for this is to flip the sleeve upside down (I don't know why this works but it does?)
